title: H.R.8250 - Parents Decide Act (119th Congress)
date_evidence: H.R.8250 - 119th Congress (2025-2026): Parents Decide Act ... introduced into Congress on April 13, 2026 ... referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce
key_claim: The Parents Decide Act (introduced 13 April 2026 by Reps Gottheimer and Stefanik) would require operating-system providers to collect a user's date of birth, require a parent or guardian to verify the age of under-18 users, and build an API allowing app developers to read the OS-held age data - moving age verification from individual sites to the device and operating-system layer.
notes: Tier 1 primary legislation; the clearest evidence of the shift to OS/device-level age verification.

title: Reddit issued with £14.47m fine for children's privacy failures
date_evidence: On February 24, 2026, the UK Information Commissioner's Office announced that Reddit, Inc. had been fined £14.47 million ... url .../2026/02/reddit-issued-with-1447m-fine...
key_claim: The UK ICO fined Reddit £14.47 million for failing to apply robust age assurance and relying on self-declaration to process under-13s' data, explicitly warning that self-declaration is not enough to protect children - signalling that verifiable age assurance is now mandatory, not optional.
notes: Tier 1 regulator enforcement. Single structural anchor (24 February 2026, ~104 days): the canonical 'self-declaration is not enough' marker.

title: The EU approach to age verification (blueprint and age-verification 'mini wallet')
date_evidence: Last update 10 March 2026 ... blueprint available 14 July 2025; enhanced second blueprint 10 October 2025; 'mini wallet' built on the same technical specifications as the European Digital Identity Wallets to be rolled out by the end of 2026
key_claim: The EU's harmonised age-verification solution (the open-source 'mini wallet') is built on the same technical specifications as the EU Digital Identity Wallet and is fully interoperable with it, lets users prove they are over 18 (or other ages, e.g. 13+) without sharing other personal data, and supports the Digital Services Act - folding age-proof into a government digital-identity layer.
notes: Tier 1 evergreen policy reference (accessed 08/06/2026); the EU's identity-wallet-based age-verification architecture.

title: Early Lessons from Australia's Teen Social Media Ban for the Rest of the World
key_claim: Australia's under-16 Social Media Minimum Age law took effect 10 December 2025; eSafety's March 2026 compliance report raised 'significant concerns' about five platforms (Facebook, Instagram, Snapchat, TikTok, YouTube), began formal investigations ahead of enforcement by mid-2026, and noted 4.7 million under-16 accounts removed or restricted by mid-January while facial age estimation showed accuracy limits near the threshold; parallel under-16/age laws are advancing in Indonesia (signed 28 March), Malaysia (June target), Austria, Brazil, India and across the EU.
notes: Tier 2 comparative policy analysis (authors are senior fellows at Atlantic Council DFRLab / Hertie); documents the global wave and the enactment-vs-enforcement gap.

title: US bill would mandate operating system-level age verification
date_evidence: US bill would mandate operating system-level age verification | Biometric Update ... url biometricupdate.com/202604/ (April 2026)
key_claim: Specialist identity-industry coverage of the Parents Decide Act framing it as mandating operating-system-level age verification, part of a broader move (alongside app-store age-assurance proposals) to push age and identity checks down into the device and platform layer.
notes: Tier 3 specialist trade press on the identity/biometrics beat; corroborates the OS/app-store identity-layer framing.

title: Meta, TikTok Flagged for Potential Australia Kids' Ban Breaches
date_evidence: Meta, TikTok Flagged for Potential Australia Kids' Ban Breaches - Bloomberg ... url bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-03-30/
key_claim: Australia's eSafety Commissioner flagged Meta, TikTok, YouTube and Snapchat for potential breaches of the under-16 ban and moved into an enforcement stance, with platforms facing fines up to A$49.5 million per breach.
notes: Tier 3 journalism; the enforcement-teeth dimension of the Australian rollout.

title: Age Verification is a Privacy Nightmare
key_claim: Every online age-verification scheme forces users to reveal sensitive personal information to third parties simply to access the web; once centralised, that data becomes an immediate target for leaks, hacks and misuse, and the mandates normalise censorship and surveillance.
verbatim_quote: users are forced to reveal sensitive personal information to third parties simply to access the web
notes: Tier 4 advocacy (stated civil-liberties position); the privacy/anonymity counter-case. Treat directionally.
